cross_references.note: §1028 criminalizes the identity theft that produces the fraudulent tradelines FCRA must block. A §1028 criminal referral + FTC identity theft report together support §1681c-2 blocking. Flores-Figueroa knowledge element and Dubin at-the-crux test apply to criminal track.

FDCPA governs debt collectors who report to CRAs. A debt collection that violates FDCPA (overshadowing, false representation, abusive communication) and is reported to a CRA compounds: §1692e false representation + §1681s-2(b) furnisher failure to correct. Dual claim opportunity.

If the fraudulent account creation or credit report manipulation involved electronic communications (email, online portal, wire transfer), §1343 wire fraud is a parallel criminal track and a civil RICO predicate. Wire fraud + FCRA violations compound the damages theory.

If multiple actors coordinated the identity theft (thief + furnisher who knows the account is fraudulent + debt collector who knows the debt is fraudulent), the pattern of racketeering activity (§1028 + §1343 predicates) supports a civil RICO claim under §1964(c). FCRA violations are not RICO predicates themselves but the underlying fraud that produces the FCRA violations may be.
Primary evidentiary source for Michael's FCRA claims. ChexSystems file + disclosure log + bank denial letters are the standing evidence chain under TransUnion.

Four contradictory Treasury responses re: bonds in Michael's name belonging to 'another individual' corroborate SSN theft. If Treasury reported to any CRA, §1681c-2 blocking available on FTC identity theft report.

FACTA §1681c-2 requires a copy of an 'identity theft report' — defined to include FTC IdentityTheft.gov reports. Filing the FTC report is the procedural trigger for the blocking right. Must be done before requesting §1681c-2 blocks from CRAs.
